decisions.label: Has A Positive Active Trade-In Value?

Flow.description:
Real gap found 2026-09-08 re-checking BRD AC2 literally: "Given a trade-in value is approved, When the Sales Representative opens the quotation, Then the trade-in value appears as a negative line item" — AF_FL_Opp_CreateQuotation only adds the Trade-In Deduction line if an Approved Appraisal already exists AT THE MOMENT the Quote is created. Since Quote creation and trade-in evaluation/approval can easily happen in either order in real use (a rep can create the Quote while the Used Car Team is still evaluating), a Trade-In approved AFTER its Opportunity's Quote already exists never got the deduction line — AC2 was only true for one specific sequencing, not "whenever approved". This flow closes that: finds the Opportunity via ReferenceRecordId, finds its existing Quote(s), and adds the same Trade-In Deduction line (same Product2/PricebookEntry as AF_FL_Opp_CreateQuotation uses) to any Quote that doesn't already have one for this specific Appraisal — safe to run even if AF_FL_Opp_CreateQuotation already added it (the AF_RelatedTradeIn__c-based existence check prevents a duplicate either way). SECOND real gap found live 2026-09-08 during a full-persona-cycle test: originally fired on AF_ApprovalStatus__c reaching Approved alone, but a validation rule (AF_VR_QLI_TradeInDeductionGate, LFRDN-630 - pre-existing in the org, not authored this session) requires the linked Trade-In to ALSO have AF_TradeInOutcome__c = "Accepted" before a Trade-In Deduction line can be created; Approved alone throws FIELD_CUSTOM_VALIDATION_EXCEPTION and blocks the Appraisal save entirely. AF_TradeInOutcome__c is described in its own field metadata as "Rep-recorded outcome" - a second, later step the initiating rep performs after Used Car Team approval (matches AF_FL_Appraisal_ApprovalApproved's own notification text: "Record the customer outcome and continue with the quotation"). Retargeted the trigger to fire on AF_TradeInOutcome__c reaching Accepted instead of AF_ApprovalStatus__c reaching Approved - this is the actually-correct BRD-consistent moment, and satisfies the validation rule's real precondition. NOTE: AF_FL_Opp_CreateQuotation (the original RS-06 flow, out of this session's scope) has the SAME latent gap - it also never checks AF_TradeInOutcome__c before creating its own inline deduction line, so a Quote created for an Opportunity whose Appraisal is Approved but not yet Accepted will also fail this validation rule. Flagged for the user, not fixed here (RS-06 is a different story). THIRD real gap found live in QA: Product2Id/PricebookEntryId for the Trade-In Deduction line were hardcoded to DEV-specific record Ids, which do not exist in QA (or any other org) - Ids are never portable across orgs. Fixed by looking up Product2 by ProductCode='AF-TRADEIN-DEDUCT' and its active PricebookEntry on the Quote's own Pricebook2Id (Get_TradeIn_Product / Get_TradeIn_PricebookEntry), instead of hardcoded literals - this is org-portable and also correctly respects a Quote on a non-Standard Pricebook, which the old hardcoded PricebookEntryId could never do. FOURTH real gap found live 2026-09-10 during a full-persona-cycle retest: the trigger only fired on ISCHANGED(AF_TradeInOutcome__c), so an Appraisal that already had AF_TradeInOutcome__c=Accepted and only later had AF_ApprovalStatus__c change to Approved (the reverse ordering from what the flow was built for) never fired at all - no future outcome change was coming to catch it. Fixed by triggering on EITHER field changing, as long as both end up in their required state (Accepted/Approved) - covers both real-world orderings symmetrically, matching how AF_FL_Opp_CreateQuotation's own Get_Approved_Appraisal lookup already checks both fields regardless of which one changed last.
2026-09-13 fixes (defects RS04-05/RS04-07, report defects #2 and #4): (a) UnitPrice was read from FinalAppraisalValue, Automotive Cloud's own platform rollup that sums every AppraisalItem regardless of approval/outcome - repointed to AF_ActiveTradeInValue__c (a declarative Roll-Up Summary of AppraisalItem.AF_ActiveValue__c, which is 0 for any item that isn't Approved+not-Declined/Withdrawn), so the line amount only ever reflects genuinely committed value. (b) When a deduction line already existed (Line_Already_Exists = true), this flow previously did nothing at all - Get_Existing_Deduction_Line found the line, and there was no branch to act on it, so a value that grew after the line was first created (e.g. a second vehicle added and approved later) was never reflected on the quote. Added Update_Existing_Deduction_Line (recordUpdate on the found line's UnitPrice) as the Already_Exists branch target, so this flow now keeps the deduction line in sync on every relevant Appraisal/AppraisalItem change, not just the first one. This flow's trigger (ISCHANGED on AF_TradeInOutcome__c or AF_ApprovalStatus__c) already re-fires whenever AF_FL_AppraisalItem_RollupOutcomeToAppraisal rewrites the parent's outcome (e.g. after a new vehicle is approved and accepted), so the revaluation now happens automatically through the existing trigger without any additional wiring.
2026-09-13 SECOND fix, found via live empirical testing (not just deploy success): the trigger's own filterFormula originally also gated on {!$Record.AF_ActiveTradeInValue__c} > 0, but AF_ActiveTradeInValue__c is a declarative Roll-Up Summary field, and its recalculation on the parent Appraisal is NOT guaranteed to have completed yet at the exact moment a same-transaction record-triggered flow (AF_FL_AppraisalItem_RollupOutcomeToAppraisal, updating this same Appraisal) causes this flow's own AfterSave trigger to evaluate - $Record reflected a stale/zero rollup value even though a direct SOQL re-query moments later showed the correct recalculated number. Confirmed live: with the value gate on $Record, the deduction line was never created at all despite every other precondition being genuinely true. Fixed by removing the value check from filterFormula (back to only ISCHANGED+Accepted+Approved) and instead re-querying the Appraisal fresh via Get_Fresh_Appraisal as the flow's first step, then gating on ITS rollup value (Has_Positive_Value) and building Formula_NegativeTradeInValue off Get_Fresh_Appraisal instead of $Record - a real SOQL query forces the rollup to be read in its current, fully-recalculated state rather than trusting the trigger context's possibly-stale snapshot.
2026-09-13 THIRD fix, also found via live empirical testing: even after the fix above, the flow STILL never fired - reproduced with a minimal isolated test (single item, single Approved+Accepted update, real Quote already present) and confirmed via a working sibling flow (AF_FL_Appraisal_ApprovalApproved, same object/trigger-type, real EmailMessage sent) that Appraisal AfterSave flows in general DO fire correctly in this org, isolating the fault to this flow's specific filterFormula. Root cause: (ISCHANGED(AF_TradeInOutcome__c) || ISCHANGED(AF_ApprovalStatus__c)) evaluated as part of a compound formula did not reliably register when BOTH fields transition from blank to their target values in the SAME update statement (the exact case exercised when AF_FL_AppraisalItem_RollupOutcomeToAppraisal writes both the parent's approval status and outcome together, and the common manual-test pattern of setting both fields in one Apex update). Confirmed by removing the ISCHANGED wrapper entirely (down to just the two ISPICKVAL checks) - the flow fired correctly and created the deduction line. Since Get_Existing_Deduction_Line / Update_Existing_Deduction_Line already makes this flow idempotent (re-running it when the fields haven't actually changed is a no-op update to the same value), dropping ISCHANGED trades a small amount of redundant execution for actually working - a strictly better trade than a filter that silently never fires. filterFormula is now just the two ISPICKVAL checks; the flow still only takes action (create or update) when a Quote and a positive active value genuinely exist.
